column5: Literal adjacent mn > βn. Fulk 2018 p.121 §6.11 and Polomé 1967 pp.818-819 support a late PGmc/Common-Germanic cluster change, not a securely PNWGmc innovation; PNWGmcMnDissimilation remains the stable Foma identifier only. The diagnostic corpus witness is stem (*stámniz > stefn); see the generated firing census for the current firing population. heaven is deeper comparative/paradigmatic evidence (ON himinn:hifni), NOT a direct row-level witness; SC022 does not fire in selected *xébun > heofon. No positive local ordering is established; the rule's executable placement is an editorial/computational holding-zone placement, not historical subgroup evidence.

General (pre-)PGmc loss of word-final *-n with nasalization (Ringe 2017 pp.101-103; proof set includes verb *dedǭ and pronoun *þanǭ; Goth. tuggo shares the weak nom.sg. outcome). Executable {*ō}{*n}-only environment is a deliberate citation-form proxy: every firing is a weak-noun citation stem in *-ōn-, and PGmc *sebun/*nigun/*tehun/*hebun retained -un (numeral analogy, Ringe 2017 p.103) and must not be touched. do is a counterfeeding (negative) witness only: OE dōn retains secondary final -n created by SC047, so the loss predates the OE apocope; stage-entailed, not a tight local adjacency. PNWGmcNStemNLoss remains the stable Foma identifier only; the rule's executable placement is an editorial/computational holding zone. See sc023-adjudication.md.

Change A of the e1 complex (re-adjudication superseding the one-step proxy): early NWGmc stressed *ē₁ > *ā in ALL environments, nasal forms included (R/T print PNWGmc *mānō, *mānōþ-, *spānuz; vol.2 pp.11-12). Pan-NWGmc, Early Runic makija later 2nd c. AD (Grønvik 1998: 87 apud R/T p.12); R/T p.13 + n.3 restrict the law to stressed syllables — executable input is the stressed tier {*ḗ} only, so the five unstressed selected-input tokens (father, mother, sister, have, live) no longer fire here and take the §6.8.3 shortening path (R/T p.147 *fadēr > *fader). Reconstruction disputed: Fulk 2018 §4.6 (low-front *ǣ retained in Anglo-Frisian), Bennett 1950: 232-235 and Grønvik retention view, Campbell §§128-129 noncommittal — confidence B. It fires on oral roots (e.g. betray) and on sow, month, spoon; see the generated firing census for the current population. Its *ā output is consumed by SC025 (nasal) and SC101 (non-nasal). Composed inside EarlyEnglishLineChanges immediately after PNWGmcAToUBeforeM, ahead of every genuinely PWGmc innovation (early i-apocope, *ij contraction, j-gemination, syllabic *j, dental hardening), matching its early pan-NWGmc dating (Early Runic makija, later 2nd c. AD). See sc024-sc025-sc101-e1-complex-adjudication.md.

ADJUDICATED (sc025-sc104-nasalized-low-vowel-adjudication.md): SPLIT. This rule now performs NASALIZATION only — inherited long *ā is nasalized before a retained nasal — and the rounding to *ō is the separate later Anglo-Frisian change SC104 EAFNasalizedLowRounding. Campbell §128 n.1 p.50 shows the intermediate was nasalized but NOT rounded, and that one later change rounded the nasalized vowel from §119, from §121 and from *ǣ alike. Scope north_sea_germanic is now correct for the nasalization specifically: Old Saxon nasalizes stressed low vowels (R/T §5.1.2 p.142) but does not share the categorical Anglo-Frisian rounding: it retains *ā consistently in the inherited PGmc nasalized-low-vowel class, while the Ingvaeonic class shows variable *ā/*ō by word and dialect (Campbell §119 p.44; Fulk §4.11 p.72). Input is the historical *ā of that stage (centrally *ā < *ē₁ via SC024). Northern West Germanic nasalization of stressed low vowels before a retained nasal is itself independently well supported (R/T §5.1.2 p.142; Campbell §119 p.44); what confidence B rates is CAPR's particular formulation *ā > *ą̄ before retained N in these forms, because identifying the input as *ā depends centrally on the disputed *ē₁ > *ā reconstruction. The rating does not transfer to SC104. Must precede SC004: displacing SC004 before this rule wrongly rounds stone/home (**stōn, **hōm). Identifier EAFLongANasalRounding kept as a stable implementation name; rename deferred to an isolated rename pass.

column5: ADJUDICATED (sc026-sc027-nasal-spirant-adjudication.md): SC026+SC027 are ONE historical sound change — the North Sea Germanic (Ingvaeonic) nasal-spirant law — implemented as two ordered transducer operations, because the vowel must be read while the conditioning nasal is still present. Domain restricted to *mf/*nþ/*ns (Campbell §121 p.47; Fulk §4.11; Sievers-Brunner §186.1; R/T §5.1.1 pp.139-41). Nasal loss before *x split out as the pan-Germanic SC103 PGmcNasalLossBeforeX (Campbell §119 p.44; Fulk §4.1); fist therefore withdrawn as a witness. Input vowels narrowed to *a/*i/*u (Fulk §4.1: e and o do not occur here). Corpus outputs unchanged.

Split out of SC026/SC027: PGmc *-Nx- > long nasalized vowel + *x, pan-Germanic (Campbell §119 p.44; Fulk §4.1 p.55; Ringe vol.1 §3.2.7(ii) pp.149-150). Comparative test: the nasal is lost in ALL daughters (OHG fūst, fūht, brāhta; Go. þūhta), unlike the Ingvaeonic law, whose witnesses keep the nasal outside the North Sea area (OHG fimf, gans, ander, jugund). Feeds SC028 PNWGmcPreconsonantalXLoss by creating the *xst cluster of fist. Nasalized-low-vowel adjudication: the low-vowel branch now outputs nasalized long *ą̄ rather than *ō — the rounding is the later Anglo-Frisian SC104 — and the rule was moved ahead of the daughter-specific NWGmc and PWGmc innovations, output-equivalently, so that a pan-Germanic change no longer follows them. Low-vowel branch witness: `thought` PGmc *θánxtē (Ringe 2017 pp. 136, 281 *þankijaną, *þanhtē, *þanhtaz) > OE þōhte, the form Fulk §4.1 p.55 itself cites for Anglo-Frisian rounding of the nasalized vowel; added 2026 because the corpus previously exercised only the high-vowel branch, through `fist`. `thought` does not feed SC028, in which respect it differs from `fist`, so it isolates SC103 > SC104.

NEW (sc025-sc104-nasalized-low-vowel-adjudication.md). One later Anglo-Frisian change rounding the long nasalized low vowel *ą̄ to *ō, with three independent feeding sources: SC103 (PGmc *aNx), SC026/SC027 (the North Sea Germanic nasal-spirant law) and SC025 (inherited long *ā before a retained nasal). Campbell §128 n.1 p.50 unifies them explicitly and shows the intermediate was unrounded (cf. samcucu, where very early shortening gives a, not o). Scope anglo_frisian: Old Saxon keeps ā invariably for the PGmc class and rounds only variably for the Ingvaeonic class (Campbell §119 p.44; Fulk §4.11 p.72). No explicit *ī̃ or *ū̃ is represented: they develop exactly like oral *ī and *ū (Campbell §121 p.47). Confidence A, independent of the disputed *ē₁ reconstruction feeding SC025.

ADJUDICATED (sc028-xs-cluster-simplification-adjudication.md): verdict RETAIN/REORDER, with restaging. The rule is not a general preconsonantal *x-loss but the *xs + consonant cluster simplification of Campbell §417 p.170 ("When a consonant follows, xs > s in OE"), Brunner §221.2 p.184 ("Wenn auf hs andere Konsonanten (auch j) folgen, ist h ausgefallen"), Bülbring §527 p.215 and R/T pp.157-158. The executable structural description was already correct and is unchanged. Three domain controls, all met by the selected corpus: *xs with no following consonant is NOT simplified but gives OE <x> = /ks/ (Campbell §416 p.170: fox, six, wax, flax, ox); *xt is NOT simplified (Campbell §464 p.186: thought, fight, night, light, might, knight, fright, wight); geminate *xx must survive as <hh> (hliehhan). The same *xst/*xt contrast is attested outside English by OHG/OS lastar < *laxstra- against OE leahtor < *laxtra-. Stage corrected from pnwgmc to pwgmc/north_wgmc: Gothic retains the *h (bi-niuhsjan, saihsta), so the change is post-PGmc, and R/T read it as a shared northern WGmc change while allowing that the North Germanic agreement may be partly parallel drift — hence confidence B for the dating, not for the existence. The former Campbell §461 citation (flēam, hēla) was a conflation with the separate OE loss of *h between vowels and between vowel and voiced consonant (Campbell §461 p.186, Bülbring §528 p.215) and has been removed. Identifier PNWGmcPreconsonantalXLoss kept as a stable implementation name; rename deferred.

column2: Later northern West Germanic loss of word-final *-z in stressed monosyllables, with compensatory lengthening of a short nucleus (*maiz > OE mā, *hwaz > hwā, *kūz > cū); OHG instead rhotacizes (ir, wir, mēr). Corpus witness: who (*xwaz > OE hwa).
column5: New rule 2026 from the SC020 three-rule split (Dossier C sc020-dossier-c-northern-monosyllable-final-z.md; adjudication memo). column5: New rule 2026 (corpus-maturation pass; dossier sc098-dossier-unstressed-word-final-i-apocope.md). Exceptionless prosodically conditioned law (R/T 2014: 57-58); apparent exceptions are proclitics outside the environment (R/T's own account). Licenses PWGmc *iuwi ~ *iuw (R/T 2014: 41-42). Fed by SC020 (z-loss makes *-i final); bleeds SC055 i-umlaut (dating evidence). Proxy environment over the SC008 geminate *ww domain, exactly coextensive with the law's unstressed-word corpus domain (cf. SC096 proxy convention). Composed after EAFFinalZDeletion, before MonosyllabicFinalZLoss.

Shortened unstressed *o (< original PWGmc *ō) > u in medial syllables. Directly demonstrated for West Saxon ō-verb pasts only: Stausland Johnsen 2015 pp.28-31, 36; witness *wúndōdē > wundude. Does not assert inherited short-*o raising or extend to Northumbrian nominal relics; see sc021-adjudication.md.
Final outcome of shortened unstressed *o (< original *ō), paired with SC099. Stausland Johnsen 2015 pp.28-31 supports the medial/final contrast; the corpus witnesses are final-syllable controls.

Change B of the e1 complex (new identity from the SC024 split): much later northern-WGmc fronting of non-nasalized stressed *ā > WS ǣ, Angl./Kent./OFris ē, sporadic OS e (R/T §5.1.2 pp.149-150). Consumes *ā < *ē₁ (SC024). The historically established *w conditioning is now encoded: fronting is blocked before *w (verba pura sāwan, cnāwan, blāwan, māwan; R/T p.151, with Hogg 1992: 81 — the simplest hypothesis is that fronting never occurred there) unless the *w is followed by high-front *i/*ī/*j, where fronting applies (*lāwijan- > lǣwan, eltǣwe, brǣw; R/T p.150). Corpus witnesses: sow (blocked, fed by SC102) vs betray (fronted at the SC101 boundary itself, not by later i-umlaut). Stated before SC004: fronting was well under way before *ai > ā completed (Campbell §132; R/T pp.169-170) — displacement after SC004 yields **lǣþ, **rǣp, **tǣcn, **sǣwol, **ġēast; displacement after SC056 yields **sċǣp, **ġǣr. See sc024-sc025-sc101-e1-complex-adjudication.md.

New identity from the sow/laewan follow-up to the e1-complex adjudication: pre-OE/Anglo-Frisian hiatus-filling *w in the vowel-final strong-verb roots (verba pura), *sāan- (< *sēaną by SC024) > *sāwan- (R/T vol.2 p.12, p.151, citing Þórhallsdóttir 1993: 82-137, known here only through R/T). Regular first before the *u-initial endings (pres.ind.1sg *-u, past ind.pl. *-un), analogically generalized through the paradigm; the executable rule is a provisional paradigm-level implementation of that outcome on citation forms ({*ā} _ V). Confidence B on its own grounds, not from the Fulk/*ē₁ dispute governing SC024/SC025/SC101: the broad innovation is supported by the scholarship consulted, but the phonological-versus-analogical architecture awaits direct adjudication from the specialist source (memo §13.4). Anglo-Frisian scope: OFris did the same (grōwinge), but OS/OHG repaired the hiatus with *j (sāian, sāen), so this is not common WGmc. Must precede SC101 — the inserted *w is what blocks fronting in sāwan (R/T p.151: early enough to prevent fronting of *ā in pre-OE); must follow PWGmc intervocalic *w-loss (R/T p.151 n.9, §3.1.5).
